title: Opus5.5 Low to Max - Bevy (rust game engine, you guys asked...)
author: 314t
selftext:
We did low to max in godot.
We did low to max in unreal.
We did low to max in three.js.
Now we have low to max in bevy.

And sorry guys, I hate bevy. I normally run these workflows in parallel, but bevy had constant memory leaks, long compilation times, and long light bake times, that is was just a bad experience overall trying to work in this engine. I had top stop my parallel runs to let one agent run at a time and finish up before starting the next, bevy just needed so much overhead. At one point, a memory leak caused bevy to shoot up to 48gb for a single scene that made my computer beg for mercy.

# Lighthouse Cabinet of Curiosities — Bevy Experimental Prototype

## Working rules for this run

- We are going to build a Bevy (Rust) project, in this folder. Rust and cargo are installed.
- Run everything headless where possible.
- Capture screenshots as needed to verify the visuals.
- Retrieve assets (download free, properly licensed ones) — do not hand-create assets.
- [my library path] may have existing assets you can reuse (see its library folder and its AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md). Check there before downloading. Copy anything you use into this project; do not modify [my library path].

## Brief

Build a scene - cabinet of curiosities inside a lighthouse during a blizzard at midnight, Edward Hopper meets Lovecraftian. Floor-to-ceiling glass cabinets (StandardMaterial with specular_transmission), specimen jars, a suspended whale skeleton, brass instruments, a reclusive collector's cluttered desk, all loaded as glTF. The lighthouse beam is a rotating SpotLight sweeping through frosted windows every 8 seconds; warm practical PointLights; chiaroscuro. Lighting: shadows on all lights, an irradiance volume or baked lightmaps for bounce light, VolumetricFog on the camera with FogVolume indoors, DistanceFog, Bloom, Tonemapping::AgX. Snow streaking outside with bevy_hanabi particles. A camera system does a slow, eased dolly push-in toward a single emissive glowing jar on the desk. Plain ECS: one plugin per concern (scene, lighting, camera, particles), no placeholders, cargo run works.
